docs.title: What is Minecraft?
docs.text:
Minecraft is a sandbox game about placing blocks, exploring, and surviving in procedurally generated worlds.

Minecraft drops you into a blocky world made of voxels. You mine resources, craft tools, build structures, and can choose how much danger you want from hostile creatures.

docs.title: Two common editions
docs.text:
• Java Edition runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It has the largest mod ecosystem and receives snapshots for upcoming features.
  • Bedrock Edition runs on consoles, mobile devices, and Windows (often via the Microsoft Store). It supports cross-play on supported platforms.

Pick the edition you own or that matches your devices. The core loop—break blocks, collect drops, craft, build—is the same idea on both.

docs.title: Game modes at a glance
docs.text:
Survival : You manage health, hunger, and inventory. Hostile mobs appear at night unless you sleep or stay well lit.

Creative : Unlimited blocks, flight, and no survival pressure—ideal for building experiments.

Peaceful (Survival option) : Survival mechanics without hostile mob spawns (you can still take environmental damage in some situations).

docs.title: Default controls (PC)
docs.text: Common keyboard and mouse bindings in Java and Bedrock on PC. Rebind keys in Options if needed.

docs.title: Movement and camera
docs.text: Input    Action    W, A, S, D    Move forward, left, back, right    Space    Jump; hold to swim up; double-tap toggles Creative flight when flying    Left Shift    Sneak \(edge of blocks, no falling off\); swim down while in water    Left Ctrl    Sprint \(consumes hunger in Survival\)    Mouse    Look around

docs.title: Interaction
docs.text: Input    Action    Left click    Attack or mine the targeted block    Right click    Use item, place block, open doors or containers    E    Open inventory \(Java default; Bedrock may differ—check Controls\)    1–9    Select hotbar slot    Q    Drop one item from the selected stack    Esc    Pause menu / close screens

docs.title: Create your first world
docs.text:
Create a new single-player world with beginner-friendly settings.

For your first session, a Survival world on Easy or Peaceful difficulty reduces pressure while you learn movement and crafting.

  1. From the title screen, choose Singleplayer, then Create New World.

  2. Enter a world name you will recognize later.

  3. Set Game Mode to Survival (or Creative if you only want to practice building).

  4. Set Difficulty to Peaceful or Easy for a gentler start.

  5. Optional: open More World Options and leave bonus chest enabled if you want starter supplies near spawn.

  6. Choose Create New World and wait for terrain generation to finish.

You spawn in the world. Note your coordinates or build a simple landmark so you can find your first base after exploring.

docs.title: Install and launch Minecraft
docs.text:
Install the launcher for your edition, sign in, and open the game.

Steps depend on whether you use Java Edition or Bedrock. Use the path that matches your purchase.

  1. Download the official launcher for your edition from minecraft.net or your platform store (for example Microsoft Store or console store).

  2. Run the installer and sign in with the Microsoft account (or Mojang account, if still in transition) linked to your license.

  3. Open the launcher, select Minecraft, then choose Play to download updates if prompted and start the game.

  4. From the main menu, confirm you can reach Singleplayer, Multiplayer, and Options. You are ready to create or join a world.

Minecraft should be installed and able to launch. If sign-in fails, verify the account that owns the game and reset the password on the official site.

docs.title: Survive your first day
docs.text:
Collect basic materials, craft essential tools, and secure shelter before nightfall.

In Survival with hostile mobs enabled, night is dangerous without light or shelter. Aim to have tools, food, and a safe place before dusk.

  1. Punch a tree to collect logs. Open your inventory and craft logs into planks, then planks into sticks.

  2. On a crafting table (four planks in a 2×2 grid in inventory, then place the table), craft a wooden pickaxe: three planks across the top row and two sticks down the middle column.

  3. Mine stone with the pickaxe and craft a stone pickaxe, then a sword if you expect combat.

  4. Gather coal or burn logs in a furnace to make charcoal for torches (stick below coal or charcoal).

  5. Build a small enclosed shelter or dig into a hillside. Place torches inside so mobs do not spawn there.

  6. Optional: craft a bed from three wool and three planks. Sleeping at night skips to dawn if no hostile mobs are nearby.

After the first night, expand your base, explore for better ores, and experiment with farming and animal breeding for steady food.
